title: Allocator confluence causing session orphaning and GPU memory surge — runtime patch
creator: Amit Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers reported intermittent GPU memory exhaustion across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments between 2025-02-12 and 2025-02-16. The root cause investigation shows a convergence of two allocator code paths that allowed session handles to become orphaned while their key-index/lookup metadata survived, producing fragmentation and leaking GPU-resident arenas. In some cases a slow probe of the per-tenant key-index caused long-lived references that prevented eviction and GC, turning small leaks into sustained memory surges.

Affected: two high-touch customers escalated (Acme Payments - Dedicated pool; Nimbus Labs - Private appliance), plus multiple Hosted customers observing latency spikes and later OOMs.

Why this is unique / high severity: This is not a single-point slab leak — it is a timing-dependent confluence in the allocator + session lifecycle that manifests as many small orphaned allocations that are difficult to reclaim. Typical eviction heuristics were not triggered because the key-index still reported live references; the allocator's arena split policy then prevented coalescing and made fragmentation permanent until process restart.

Reproduction notes: We can reproduce under controlled load with the provided harness by running 200 concurrent multi-turn chat sessions, enabling prefix-cache with disabled aggressive-eviction, and toggling session-handles to force race window (see repro steps below). Repro runs show progressive rise in resident set and GPU memory map fragmentation metrics within 20–40 minutes.
diagnostics: Heap histogram shows many ~64KB GPU allocations attributed to 'session-key-map' namespace
GPU pmap snapshots show increasing number of non-contiguous extents over time (fragmentation ratio > 0.48)
Logs contain repeated traces of "allocation attempt -> fallback slab -> recorded reference removed from session struct but present in key-index" across allocator and session manager stacks
KV-like index (internal name: key-indexer) reported references while the session-store had removed the handle (race window visible at UTC timestamps)
Canary runs with arena-coalesce disabled reproduced failure consistently; enabling aggressive coalesce reduced memory growth but didn't fully remediate
actions_taken: 2025-02-16 04:12 UTC: Opened escalations with Acme Payments / Nimbus Labs and collected heap dumps and kube node snapshots
2025-02-17 09:40 UTC: Rolled emergency mitigation (runtime flag runtime.eviction.force_compact=true) to affected Hosted region to buy breathing room
2025-02-18 02:20 UTC: Added diagnostic tracing to session lifecycle to capture orphan window (PR #runtime/1342) — limited perf cost, enabled on canary only
2025-02-20 18:00 UTC: Developed and QA'd runtime patch 'arena-fanout-safe-evictor' that serializes allocator coalescing with session teardown to ensure no orphaned references remain
2025-02-22 02:45 UTC: Canary rollout of runtime-1.20 with patch to 10% of Hosted capacity and one Dedicated customer (non-production) — monitor dashboards show reduced fragmentation growth
2025-02-24 12:30 UTC: Hotfix PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1473 opened for backport to 1.18 and 1.19 branches
2025-02-25 06:00 UTC: Manual remediation playbook executed for Acme Payments node group: graceful drain + restart + post-restart compaction, which restored normal memory levels
2025-02-26 22:00 UTC: Provided Nimbus Labs on-prem appliance with a signed patch bundle and step-by-step remediation playbook; they reported initial stabilization after restart and compaction
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): runtime-1.20 with arena-fanout-safe-evictor to 10% Hosted capacity + dedicated QA nodes — duration 72h
Phase 1 (limited roll): 50% Hosted capacity + one Dedicated customer pool + delayed Private appliance image for partner validation — duration 72h
Phase 2 (full roll): all Hosted regions + Dedicated clusters and release image to Private customers via secure channel
Backout plan: revert runtime flag + coordinate rolling restart of nodes if fragmentation persists; emergency fallback to 'eviction.force_compact' for short-term relief
postmortem_notes: Root cause: race between session teardown and key-index clearing combined with allocator arena split/coalesce policy

Why earlier safeguards failed: eviction heuristics used key-index liveness which could be transiently inconsistent during teardown; allocator didn't coalesce across split boundaries without explicit synchronization

Corrective measures: patch enforces a lightweight rendezvous during session destroy that blocks coalesce until the key-index has drained, adds a safety tracer counter that fires automated compaction if orphan-window exceeds threshold
Action items added to backlog: separate smaller tickets for eviction tuning, monitoring alerting for fragmentation ratio, and allocator unit tests to simulate session race windows
next_steps: Finish canary 72h monitoring and collect fragmentation metrics for pre/post comparison
Backport approved hotfixes to runtime-1.18 and runtime-1.19 and schedule low-risk maintenance window for Dedicated customers
Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to run appliance patch at two Private pilot customers; verify on-site compaction steps
Add synthetic smoke tests to CI that emulate the session-handle race window and assert no leaked GPU allocations remain
Automate playbook steps for forced compaction via operator CLI to reduce manual toil
notes: Engineering lead: pair of backend + allocator engineers assigned to 3-day on-call rotation for real-time monitoring
Customer comms: GTM and Support coordinated a status email to affected tenants and posted incident updates to the status page
Risk consideration: patch introduces a short critical section in the allocator; perf microbenchmarks show ~0.6% median latency change under typical loads — acceptable under P0 constraints
